extracted.intended_audience: journalists, newsroom editors, and media professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Core ethical principles and specific practice standards for journalists producing news: guidance on seeking truth, minimizing harm, maintaining independence, and being accountable to the public. Intended to govern behavior and decision-making across reporting, editing, and news production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preamble: duty of the journalist
rubrics_metrics.description: Members ... believe that public enlightenment is the forerunner of justice and the foundation of democracy. The duty of the journalist is to further those ends by seeking truth and providing a fair and comprehensive account of events and issues. Professional integrity is the cornerstone of a journalist's credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the code's purpose: public enlightenment, truth-seeking, fairness, comprehensiveness, and professional integrity as foundational values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek Truth and Report It (overall)
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists should be honest, fair and courageous in gathering, reporting and interpreting information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the broad mandate guiding the specific practices listed below (accuracy testing, source identification, avoiding distortion, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Test accuracy of information
rubrics_metrics.description: Test the accuracy of information from all sources and exercise care to avoid inadvertent error. Deliberate distortion is never permissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actively verify facts from multiple sources when possible; avoid inadvertent mistakes and never intentionally distort facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diligently seek response from subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Diligently seek out subjects of news stories to give them the opportunity to respond to allegations of wrongdoing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make reasonable efforts to contact and include responses from people accused or implicated before publishing allegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify sources whenever feasible
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify sources whenever feasible. The public is entitled to as much information as possible on sources' reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer named sources; when anonymity is used, provide context on source reliability and reasons for anonymity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question motives before promising anonymity
rubrics_metrics.description: Always question sources' motives before promising anonymity. Clarify conditions attached to any promise made in exchange for information. Keep promises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess why a source seeks anonymity, set clear terms, and honor promises given to sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid misrepresentation in headlines and promos
rubrics_metrics.description: Make certain that headlines, news teases and promotional material, photos, video, audio, graphics, sound bites and quotations do not misrepresent. They should not oversimplify or highlight incidents out of context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that ancillary materials accurately reflect the story and do not create misleading impressions through truncation or out-of-context emphasis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not distort photos or video
rubrics_metrics.description: Never distort the content of news photos or video. Image enhancement for technical clarity is always permissible. Label montages and photo illustrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow technical corrections (clarity) but prohibit content-altering edits; clearly label composites and illustrative images.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid misleading reenactments; label if necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid misleading re-enactments or staged news events. If re-enactment is necessary to tell a story, label it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not present staged material as factual; when reenactment is used, make the nature of the material explicit to the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use undercover methods only as last resort
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid undercover or other surreptitious methods of gathering information except when traditional open methods will not yield information vital to the public. Use of such methods should be explained as part of the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reserve secret-gathering techniques for situations where public interest justifies intrusion and explain why they were necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Never plagiarize
rubrics_metrics.description: Never plagiarize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attribute and credit others' work; do not present others' words or ideas as your own.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tell diverse human stories boldly
rubrics_metrics.description: Tell the story of the diversity and magnitude of the human experience boldly, even when it is unpopular to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover a broad range of voices and experiences, including those that may be controversial or marginalized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine and avoid imposing cultural values
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine their own cultural values and avoid imposing those values on others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflect on personal biases and avoid ethnocentric judgments when reporting on other cultures or communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid stereotyping
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid stereotyping by race, gender, age, religion, ethnicity, geography, sexual orientation, disability, physical appearance or social status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful in language, selection of sources, and portrayal to prevent reinforcing harmful stereotypes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support open exchange of views
rubrics_metrics.description: Support the open exchange of views, even views they find repugnant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow and fairly cover a range of perspectives rather than excluding unpopular or offensive viewpoints solely for being unpopular.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give voice to the voiceless
rubrics_metrics.description: Give voice to the voiceless; official and unofficial sources of information can be equally valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include perspectives from marginalized or less-heard individuals and communities, evaluating credibility on merit, not status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish advocacy from news reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish between advocacy and news reporting. Analysis and commentary should be labeled and not misrepresent fact or context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly label opinion, analysis, and advocacy; avoid presenting advocacy as objective news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish news from advertising
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish news from advertising and shun hybrids that blur the lines between the two.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid advertorial content or sponsored material that could be mistaken for independent reporting; maintain clear separation of editorial and commercial content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure government openness and records access
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize a special obligation to ensure that the public's business is conducted in the open and that government records are open to inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate for transparency, use public records in reporting, and challenge secrecy when public interest is implicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize Harm (overall)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethical journalists treat sources, subjects and colleagues as human beings deserving of respect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This section frames duties to consider the effects of reporting on people and to exercise compassion and restraint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show compassion for affected people
rubrics_metrics.description: Show compassion for those who may be affected adversely by news coverage. Use special sensitivity when dealing with children and inexperienced sources or subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take extra care with vulnerable populations; adapt interview techniques and presentation to avoid additional harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be sensitive when using interviews/photographs of grieving people
rubrics_metrics.description: Be sensitive when seeking or using interviews or photographs of those affected by tragedy or grief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid intrusive or exploitative approaches during times of trauma; consider timing and method of contact and publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize reporting can cause harm; avoid arrogance
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that gathering and reporting information may cause harm or discomfort. Pursuit of the news is not a license for arrogance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh public interest against potential harm; do not use the excuse of reporting to justify disrespectful or harmful conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect privacy of private individuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that private people have a greater right to control information about themselves than do public officials and others who seek power, influence or attention. Only an overriding public need can justify intrusion into anyone's privacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate between private persons and public figures; intrude on privacy only when public interest outweighs harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show good taste; avoid pandering to lurid curiosity
rubrics_metrics.description: Show good taste. Avoid pandering to lurid curiosity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid sensationalism and gratuitous detail that serves only to titillate rather than inform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be cautious identifying juveniles and sex crime victims
rubrics_metrics.description: Be cautious about identifying juvenile suspects or victims of sex crimes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect identities where appropriate, mindful of legal and ethical considerations concerning minors and victims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be judicious naming criminal suspects before charges
rubrics_metrics.description: Be judicious about naming criminal suspects before the formal filing of charges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid prematurely naming suspects in ways that could harm reputations before due process; balance with public's right to know.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance fair trial rights with public's right to be informed
rubrics_metrics.description: Balance a criminal suspect's fair trial rights with the public's right to be informed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the potential impact of coverage on judicial fairness and ongoing legal proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act Independently (overall)
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists should be free of obligation to any interest other than the public's right to know.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This section emphasizes independence from outside influences and conflicts of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid conflicts of interest, real or perceived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recuse yourself or disclose relationships that could compromise impartiality or the appearance of impartiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remain free of compromising associations
rubrics_metrics.description: Remain free of associations and activities that may compromise integrity or damage credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid memberships or activities that could call into question an individual's ability to report objectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refuse gifts and special treatment that compromise integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Refuse gifts, favors, fees, free travel and special treatment, and shun secondary employment, political involvement, public office and service in community organizations if they compromise journalistic integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decline perks or outside work that create obligations or influence reporting; preserve independence from those covered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose unavoidable conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose unavoidable conflicts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When conflicts cannot be avoided, be transparent with editors and the public about their nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hold the powerful accountable
rubrics_metrics.description: Be vigilant and courageous about holding those with power accountable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize investigative work and scrutiny of officials and institutions regardless of pressure or intimidation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deny favored treatment to advertisers and special interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Deny favored treatment to advertisers and special interests and resist their pressure to influence news coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain editorial independence when commercial pressures arise; ensure coverage is not biased by advertisers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid buying information or bidding for news
rubrics_metrics.description: Be wary of sources offering information for favors or money, avoid bidding for news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not create perverse incentives or pay for news in ways that compromise accuracy or independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be Accountable (overall)
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists are accountable to their readers, listeners, viewers and each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame for obligations around transparency, correction, and responsiveness to the public and colleagues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify coverage and invite dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify and explain news coverage and invite dialogue with the public over journalistic conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain reporting choices, sourcing, and methodology; engage audiences in discussions about journalistic practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage public grievances
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage the public to voice grievances against the news media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide accessible channels for complaints and feedback and take them seriously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admit and correct mistakes promptly
rubrics_metrics.description: Admit mistakes and correct them promptly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge errors openly, issue corrections or clarifications quickly and visibly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expose unethical media practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Expose unethical practices of journalists and the news media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate and report on misconduct in journalism with the same rigor applied to other institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abide by same standards held for others
rubrics_metrics.description: Abide by the same high standards to which they hold others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply ethical rules consistently to one's own work and behavior as to those being reported on.
